rationale.Physical Exam: General Appearance: The general examination is extremely useful to determine how sick the patient looks.
rationale.Physical Exam: Chest / Lungs: It's important to rule out any lung issues such as metastatic disease.
rationale.Physical Exam: Abdomen: Abdominal pathology can present as pelvic pain. Example: inflammatory bowel disease.
rationale.Physical Exam: Genitalia: Important since the source of pain is coming from the pelvic area.
rationale.CT/MRI/US abdomen/pelvis: CT would give diagnosis of endometrioma. Pelvic US (transvaginal) is typically first-line.
rationale.Laparotomy / Laparoscopy / Consult OB/GY: The endometrioma should be surgically removed. OB/GYN consult is appropriate.
rationale.Instruct patient, smoking cessation: One of the most important things patients can do for their health is to stop smoking.
rationale.Advise patient, no illegal drug use: Good opportunity to discuss the medical effects of cannabis use.
rationale.Appendectomy: While appendicitis can present with RLQ pain, imaging shows adnexal mass consistent with endometrioma. Gynecologic consult is correct.
rationale.Broad-spectrum antibiotics (without cult: No evidence of infection. Tuboovarian abscess is on the differential but imaging should guide therapy.
rationale.Discharge home without follow-up: Patient has a surgical adnexal mass requiring OB/GYN consultation and likely operative management.

hpi: {{patient_name}} is a reproductive-age woman who presents with severe pelvic pain that worsens with sexual activity. The pain is localized to the right adnexal region. Differential for a right adnexal mass in a reproductive-age female is broad and includes ectopic pregnancy, tuboovarian abscess, inflammatory bowel disease, ovarian mass, endometrioma, theca lutein cysts, and germ cell neoplasms. Imaging and appropriate surgical consultation are required.
